original_question: For which natural numbers n does there exist a field F whose Brauer group has exactly n elements?
target_in_paper: Problem 11.5 in §11.D (The Brumer–Rosen Conjecture): For which natural numbers n is there a field F such that |Br(F)| = n? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target almost verbatim: it asks for those natural numbers n for which there exists a field F whose Brauer group has exactly n elements. In the paper's notation, this is the classical Brauer group Br(F). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question fully self-contained in the paper's notation, identify the group explicitly as the classical Brauer group Br(F). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
Write the cardinality condition explicitly as |Br(F)| = n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
Make clear that F ranges over arbitrary fields; Problem 11.5 imposes no extra hypotheses on characteristic, roots of unity, or finiteness. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

If you want to remove ambiguity about whether 0 is counted as a natural number, say 'positive integers n'; this is a presentational clarification, since the paper simply says 'natural numbers.' ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
refined_question: For which positive integers n does there exist a field F such that the classical Brauer group Br(F) has exactly n elements, i.e. |Br(F)| = n?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting §11.D rather than the paper's early crossed-product problems: it coincides with Problem 11.5 almost word for word. The surrounding context confirms this identification: the authors introduce the question after observing that R and iterated Laurent-series fields are the familiar examples with finite nonzero Brauer group, then immediately explain that the finer Brumer–Rosen Conjecture 11.6 would imply that the only finite possibilities are powers of 2, and they note that Fein and Schacher showed every power of 2 can occur. That nearby discussion gives the intended motivation, but the official formulation to preserve is still exactly the existence/classification question for the finite cardinality of Br(F). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
